threads.subject: How to configure SPARQL endpoint in VocBench?

messages.author: John Smith
messages.subject: How to configure SPARQL endpoint in VocBench?
messages.body: Hi everyone, I'm new to VocBench and trying to configure a custom SPARQL endpoint. I have an existing GraphDB instance and want to connect VocBench to it. Can someone guide me through the process?

messages.author: Jane Doe
messages.subject: Re: How to configure SPARQL endpoint in VocBench?
messages.body:
Hello John! To configure a SPARQL endpoint in VocBench:
1. Go to Administration > Project Settings
2. Navigate to the 'Data Access' section
3. Select 'Remote Repository' option
4. Enter your GraphDB SPARQL endpoint URL (usually http://localhost:7200/repositories/your-repo)
5. Test the connection and save

Make sure your GraphDB instance is running and accessible.

messages.author: John Smith
messages.subject: Re: How to configure SPARQL endpoint in VocBench?
messages.body: Thank you Jane! That worked perfectly. I was looking in the wrong settings menu.

messages.author: Alice Johnson
messages.subject: Error importing SKOS vocabulary
messages.body:
I'm trying to import an existing SKOS vocabulary (RDF/XML format) into VocBench, but I keep getting a parsing error. The file validates fine in Protégé. Any ideas?

Error message: 'Invalid RDF/XML syntax at line 145'

messages.author: Bob Wilson
messages.subject: Re: Error importing SKOS vocabulary
messages.body: Hi Alice, could you check if your RDF/XML file has any special characters or namespace issues? VocBench can be strict about namespace declarations. Try validating with the W3C RDF Validator first.

messages.author: VocBench Support
messages.subject: Re: Error importing SKOS vocabulary
messages.body:
Alice, in addition to Bob's suggestion, you might want to:
1. Try converting to Turtle format first
2. Check if there are any blank nodes that might be causing issues
3. Look at line 145 specifically - sometimes it's a malformed literal or language tag
4. Make sure all required SKOS namespaces are declared

If the problem persists, feel free to share a sample of the problematic section.

messages.author: Alice Johnson
messages.subject: Re: Error importing SKOS vocabulary
messages.body: Thanks everyone! The issue was a language tag with an underscore instead of a hyphen (en_US vs en-US). Fixed it and the import works now!

messages.author: Carlos Martinez
messages.subject: Best practices for collaborative editing
messages.body: We have a team of 5 people working on the same vocabulary in VocBench. What are the best practices for collaborative editing? Should we use different user roles? How do we handle conflicts?

messages.author: VocBench Support
messages.subject: Re: Best practices for collaborative editing
messages.body:
Great question Carlos! Here are some best practices:

1. **Use Validation Workflow**: Enable the validation workflow where editors propose changes and validators approve them
2. **Assign Roles**: Use VocBench's role system - Editors, Validators, and Project Managers
3. **Use Groups**: Organize your team into groups if working on different concept schemes
4. **Change Tracking**: VocBench tracks all changes with timestamps and user info
5. **Regular Communication**: Establish conventions for concept labels and definitions
6. **Branching**: For major changes, consider using VocBench's branching feature

Conflicts are minimized by VocBench's transaction system, but communication is key!

messages.author: Diana Lee
messages.subject: Re: Best practices for collaborative editing
messages.body: We've been using VocBench with a team of 8 for the past year. The validation workflow is essential! Also recommend setting up regular sync meetings to discuss complex modeling decisions. The history view is great for understanding who changed what and why.

messages.author: Grace Taylor
messages.subject: Exporting to different RDF formats
messages.body: What's the recommended way to export a vocabulary from VocBench in different RDF formats? I need Turtle, JSON-LD, and RDF/XML versions of the same vocabulary for different use cases.

messages.author: Henry Brown
messages.subject: Re: Exporting to different RDF formats
messages.body:
Grace, you can export in multiple formats:

1. Go to Data > Export
2. Select your export scope (whole project, specific scheme, etc.)
3. Choose the format from the dropdown (Turtle, RDF/XML, JSON-LD, N-Triples, etc.)
4. Click export and download

You can repeat this process for each format you need. VocBench uses the same underlying RDF model, so all exports will be semantically equivalent.

messages.author: Grace Taylor
messages.subject: Re: Exporting to different RDF formats
messages.body: Perfect, thanks Henry! I found it. One more question - is there a way to automate this via API? We might want to set up automated exports on a schedule.
